results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database, which describes the mushroom body as divided into these three parts: the calyx, which receives sensory interneuron afferents, the pedunculus, a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes, and the mushroom body lobe system, consisting of a vertical branch and a medial branch that have different structures at different life stages. VFB holds two records that confirm this subdivision.

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response: The adult Drosophila brain contains several types of Kenyon cells. VFB records show that these include [KCab-c(i)](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049111 "Open [KCab-c](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00110929 "Open KCab-c in Virtual Fly Brain")(i) in Virtual Fly Brain"), KCab-c, [KCg-m](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111061 "Open KCg-m in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Kenyon cell of main calyx](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047926 "Open [Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain") of main calyx in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [gamma Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100247 "Open gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"). Additionally, VFB data indicates that Kenyon cells can be classified into alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells, which are further subdivided into subtypes such as core/surface/posterior, anterior-posterior/middle, and dorsal/main/gamma-s/gamma-t classes. VFB holds [37](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of Kenyon cell") subclasses of Kenyon cell.

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response:
The [lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111763 "Open lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2 in Virtual Fly Brain") is a type of visual neuron located in the dorsal area of the lateral cell body rind. It has distinct dendritic arbors in each lobula plate layer, extending outwards from the main fiber in the direction of motion detection for the layer. In the lobula, its main dendritic arbors are found in layers 4 and 5B, with minor processes in layer 5A, and presynaptic sites in layer 4. The lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2 projects to an optic glomerulus of the PVLP, anterior to LPLC1 and dorsal to LC4. 

Its function is to detect looming stimuli, which elicits a jump escape response. The lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2 is cholinergic and approximately 80 of these cells are found per optic lobe. VFB records show that the arbors of the lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2 span approximately 25 lobula optic columns, overlapping with other LPLC2 cells. 

The information on the lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2 comes from VFB, which summarizes neuron profiles and provides term information, citing publications by Wu et al., 2016, Klapoetke et al., 2017, Tanaka and Clark, 2022, and Davis et al., 2020.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior and has a unique anatomy and connectivity. It is characterized by its large cell body, located posterior to the lower protocerebrum, and its large descending axon, which is several times larger than any other axon in the cervical connective. The axon enters the cervical connective via the posterior cerebro-cervical fascicle and descends on the ipsilateral side, in the dorsal cervical fasciculus. In the brain, the giant fiber neuron has dendritic arborization in the ipsilateral zones A and B of the antennal mechanosensory and motor center, where it receives substantial input from zone A and B Johnston organ neurons. It also arborizes in the posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum and gorget. 

The giant fiber neuron extends posteroventrally to the mesothoracic neuromere, where it turns ventrolaterally, and ends abruptly without branching. In the mesothoracic neuromere, it forms electrical synapses with downstream motor and premotor neurons at the inframedial bridge, where the two giant fiber neurons connect across the midline, and at the axonal lateral bend. The giant fiber neuron is a [primary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047097 "Open primary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain").

Available driver lines for the giant fiber neuron include: P{R48A11-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R30C01-p65.AD}, P{R68A06-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R25C08-p65.AD}, P{R79H02-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R14A01-p65.AD}, P{R79H02-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R25C08-p65.AD}, P{VT004455-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R10A12-p65.AD}. 

Relevant publications on the giant fiber neuron include those by Phelan et al., 1996, King and Wyman, 1980, Stürner et al., 2025, Dorkenwald et al., 2024, Namiki et al., 2018, Thomas and Wyman, 1984, Koto et al., 1981, Power, 1948, Ito et al., 2014, Kamikouchi et al., 2009, Kennedy and Broadie, 2018, Allen et al., 1998, Bacon and Strausfeld, 1986, Matsuo et al., 2016, Kim et al., 2020. 

VFB holds records showing the giant fiber neuron is connected to various other neuron types, including [adult VNC neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00059289 "Open adult VNC neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [thoracic neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00001983 "Open thoracic neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), primary neuron, and [input/output neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00053396 "Open input/output neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"). However, the full set of connectivity partners is not specified here; for a comprehensive list, further queries of the VFB database would be necessary.
